notes.content:
**Executive summary:** Two late-18th-century revolutions spread the ideas of **equality, freedom and democracy**.
• **American Revolution** — 13 colonies **rejected colonial rule** and chose democracy → **USA**.
• **French Revolution** — caused by social, religious and economic **injustice** → **end of monarchy** in France.

| | American Revolution | French Revolution |
|---|---|---|
| Against | British colonial rule | Absolute monarchy & privileged Estates |
| Key year | 1776 Declaration of Independence | 1789 Storming of the Bastille |
| Result | USA (Treaty of Paris 1783) | Republic (1792); rise of Napoleon |
| Common ideas | Liberty, equality, government by consent | Liberty, equality, fraternity |

fiveW.who: 13 British colonies in North America vs the British Parliament and King
fiveW.what: Growing conflict over taxes and self-rule
fiveW.why: Heavy taxes and trade restrictions without representation in Parliament
fiveW.how: Boycotts, protests, the Boston Tea Party, Continental Congress

notes.content:
• **13 British colonies** on the Atlantic coast by **1733**; each had an elected assembly, but **governors were appointed by Britain**.
• Colonists were prosperous and independent, with flourishing overseas trade.
• Britain claimed colonial profits; imposed **heavy taxes** and **economic restrictions**.
• By **1763** Britain held vast American territories and wanted colonies to pay for defence.
• Slogan: **'No taxation without representation'** — colonists demanded seats in the British Parliament.
• More tax Acts → **boycott of British goods**.
• **Boston Massacre (5 March 1770)** — British soldiers fired on a mob in Boston, killing civilians.

notes.subtopic: 3. Boston Tea Party, Intolerable Acts, Continental Congress

fiveW.who: American revolutionaries vs the English East India Company and Britain
fiveW.what: 342 chests of tea dumped into the harbour; Britain retaliated
fiveW.why: Protest against the tea tax and the EIC's monopoly
fiveW.how: Revolutionaries boarded EIC ships; Britain passed punitive laws; colonies united in Congress

notes.content:
**Boston Tea Party (16 Dec 1773):** revolutionaries boarded EIC ships and dumped **342 chests of tea** — protest against the **tax on tea** and the **EIC's monopoly**.

**Intolerable Acts (1774):** harsh punitive laws to punish **Massachusetts** — took away self-government and **closed Boston Harbour** until the EIC was repaid.

**First Continental Congress (Sept 1774, Philadelphia):** delegates from **12 colonies**; decided to **boycott British goods** and ban trade unless the Acts were repealed; set up the **Continental Association**.

**Second Continental Congress (May 1775, Philadelphia)** — after Lexington and Concord.

**Now:** the 21st-century US **Tea Party Movement** (anti-tax) takes its name from 1773.

notes.subtopic: 4. War, Declaration of Independence, Treaty of Paris

fiveW.who: George Washington (commander); Jefferson, Adams, Franklin, Sherman, Livingston (Declaration)
fiveW.where: Lexington, Concord, Bunker Hill (Massachusetts); Philadelphia; Paris
fiveW.what: War of Independence → birth of the USA
fiveW.how: Colonial army fought Britain; Declaration adopted; Treaty of Paris recognised independence

notes.content:
• **April 1775 — Battles of Lexington and Concord** (British force vs colonial militia).
• **June 1775 — Battle of Bunker Hill** (Breed's Hill) — first major battle.
• **George Washington** chosen commander-in-chief.

**Declaration of Independence — 4 July 1776**
• Committee (formed 11 June 1776): **Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Roger Sherman, Robert R. Livingston**.
• Proclaimed **all men are born equal** with equal rights; **government by consent of the governed**.
• 4 July = US **Independence Day**; a model for other colonies.

**Treaty of Paris (1783)** — Britain recognised independence → **United States of America**.
• **1789** — Washington elected **first President**.
• **1791** — **Bill of Rights** (first 10 amendments) — model for constitutions worldwide.

**Three Estates**
| Estate | Members | Status |
|---|---|---|
| First | **Clergy** | Privileged |
| Second | **Nobles** and families | Privileged |
| Third | **Peasants, artisans, bourgeoisie** (professionals, traders) | Paid all taxes |

**Privileges of the first two Estates:** command of army and top government posts · **exemption from direct taxes** · right to oppose the king's taxes on landowners. Most farmland was owned by nobles and clergy.

**Caricature (primary source):** an old peasant carrying a clergyman and a noble on his back = the **Third Estate bearing the burden** of the privileged.

fiveW.who: Third Estate led by the bourgeoisie vs King Louis XVI and the privileged Estates
fiveW.when: Build-up in the 18th century; broke out 1789
fiveW.why: Inequality, bankruptcy, extravagance, absolute rule, ideas of philosophers, American example
fiveW.how: The Third Estate formed the National Assembly and the people rose in revolt

notes.content:
• **Philosophers — Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau** — exposed injustice; gave the slogan **Liberty, Equality, Fraternity**.
• **Influence of the American Revolution** — French soldiers returned inspired.
• **Wars since Louis XIV** emptied the treasury.
• **Extravagance** of **Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette**.
• **Absolute monarchy** — the king's word was law.
• **Bankruptcy** → new taxes; **corrupt, inefficient administration**.
• Nobles refused land tax → the **whole tax burden fell on the Third Estate** (even on **salt**); the rich **bourgeoisie lacked political rights** and led the revolution.
• **Immediate cause:** near-collapse of government finances; bad harvests → **food shortage, high prices, unemployment**.

fiveW.who: Third Estate/National Assembly, Paris crowds; Louis XVI, Marie Antoinette
fiveW.what: Oath, Storming of the Bastille, Rights of Man, Republic, execution of the king
fiveW.why: To end autocracy and privilege, and secure rights
fiveW.how: Assembly vowed a constitution; the mob freed Bastille prisoners; the Convention abolished monarchy

notes.content:
• **June 1789 — Tennis Court Oath:** Third Estate formed the **National Assembly**; at a tennis court in **Versailles** vowed to make a **new constitution**.
• **14 July 1789 — Storming of the Bastille:** political prison and symbol of autocracy; prisoners freed — **turning point**.
• **Sept 1789 — Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen**; new constitution by **1791**.
• **1792 — National Convention abolished monarchy**; **French Republic** declared.
• **1793 — Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette guillotined** in Paris.

notes.subtopic: 8. Results and Influence of the French Revolution
notes.content:
**Results**
• End of **absolute monarchy**; France became a **republic**.
• **Liberty, equality, fraternity** — guiding principles.
• **Democratic government** — people helped make laws.
• **Power of the Church curbed**.
• Popularised **nationalism**.
• Welfare reforms.
• **Rise of Napoleon Bonaparte**.

**Influence:** people across Europe revolted against autocrats; **democracy** spread; mass movements worldwide.

**India link:** our **Preamble** contains **Liberty, Equality, Fraternity** — inspired by the French Revolution.

fiveW.where: Born Corsica; wars across Europe; exiled to Elba and St. Helena
fiveW.what: Rose from army officer to Emperor Napoleon I; dominated Europe
fiveW.why: Military genius, quick decisions, post-Revolution instability
fiveW.how: Coup against the Directory, Napoleonic Wars, defeated by a coalition

notes.content:
• Born **1769, Corsica**; lieutenant in **1785**.
• **1799** — coup d'état overthrew the **Directory**; **Consulate** set up.
• Became **Emperor Napoleon I**; **Napoleonic Wars** against every major European power.
• **1805 — Battle of Austerlitz**: defeated **Austria and Russia**.
• **1806** Prussia, **1807** Russia defeated; by **1810** he dominated most of Europe.
• **1813 — Leipzig**: defeated by a coalition of **Britain, Austria, Prussia**.
• **1814** — exiled to **Elba**; escaped.
• **1815 — Battle of Waterloo**: final defeat.
• Died **1821** on **St. Helena** under British supervision.

questions.question: What is 'No taxation without representation'?
questions.answer: A slogan of the American colonists (1750s–60s). Britain taxed the colonies but they had no representatives in the British Parliament; they argued that without representation Britain had no right to tax them, and demanded self-governance.

questions.question: What was the Boston Massacre?
questions.answer: On 5 March 1770, a large mob gathered around British soldiers in Boston; the soldiers fired into the crowd, killing civilians. It intensified the colonists' demand to govern themselves.

questions.question: (a) What were the Intolerable Acts? (b) Describe the Boston Tea Party. (c) Discuss the beginning of military hostilities.
questions.answer:
• (a) Intolerable Acts (1774): harsh punitive laws to punish Massachusetts for the Tea Party — ended self-government and closed Boston Harbour until the EIC was repaid.
  • (b) Boston Tea Party (16 Dec 1773): revolutionaries boarded EIC ships and dumped 342 chests of tea to protest the tea tax and the EIC monopoly.
  • (c) Hostilities: April 1775 — Lexington and Concord; June 1775 — Bunker Hill; colonists formed an army under George Washington.

questions.question: Why was the Declaration of Independence called a revolutionary document?
questions.answer:
• Adopted on 4 July 1776; asserted the colonists' right to free themselves from British rule.
  • Proclaimed that all men are born equal with equal rights.
  • Based on government by consent of the governed — practised by no other country then; became a model for colonies seeking freedom.

questions.question: Name two French philosophers who played a major role in the revolutionary movement. What was their contribution?
questions.answer: Voltaire and Rousseau (also Montesquieu). Their writings exposed injustice in French society and politics and inspired the middle class with ideas of liberty, equality and fraternity.

questions.question: Explain the causes of the French Revolution.
questions.answer:
• Social inequality: privileged First and Second Estates paid no direct tax; the Third Estate bore all taxes, even on salt.
  • Political: absolute monarchy — the king's word was law; corrupt administration.
  • Economic: wars since Louis XIV and the extravagance of Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette → bankruptcy → new taxes.
  • Intellectual: Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau.
  • American Revolution inspired French soldiers.
  • Immediate: near-collapse of finances; bad harvests → food shortage, high prices, unemployment.
questions.topperTip: Use Social / Political / Economic / Intellectual / Immediate headings — instant structure.

questions.question: How did the Third Estate suffer? Who formed French society before the Revolution?
questions.answer:
• Suffering: nobles refused the land tax, so the entire tax burden fell on the Third Estate — taxed on everything, including salt; denied privileges; poor peasants worst hit; the bourgeoisie had wealth but no political rights.
  • Society: First Estate — clergy; Second Estate — nobles; Third Estate — peasants, artisans, bourgeoisie.

questions.question: What was the Tennis Court Oath?
questions.answer: In June 1789, the Third Estate formed the National Assembly. Its members gathered in the Tennis Court at Versailles and swore to frame a new constitution and a national government representing all the people.

questions.question: Why was the Storming of the Bastille significant?
questions.answer:
• The Bastille was a political prison and a symbol of French autocracy.
  • On 14 July 1789 an angry crowd stormed it and freed the prisoners.
  • It was the turning point of the revolution — a vigorous rejection of monarchical rule.

questions.question: Why is the French Revolution an important landmark in world history?
questions.answer:
• Ended absolute monarchy and privilege by birth.
  • Gave the world liberty, equality and fraternity.
  • Spread democracy and nationalism; people across Europe rose against autocrats.
  • Inspired mass movements worldwide — even India's Preamble carries its ideals.
questions.topperTip: Linking to the Indian Preamble is a distinctive topper touch.

questions.question: Write a note on Napoleon Bonaparte.
questions.answer:
• Born 1769 in Corsica; lieutenant in the French army in 1785; rose through quick decisions and ability.
  • 1799: coup against the Directory → Consulate; later Emperor Napoleon I.
  • Napoleonic Wars: Austerlitz 1805 (Austria, Russia); Prussia 1806; Russia 1807; dominated Europe by 1810.
  • Fall: Leipzig 1813 → exiled to Elba 1814 → escaped → Waterloo 1815 → died on St. Helena 1821.
questions.topperTip: Write it as Rise → Height → Fall with dates.

questions.question: Battle of Austerlitz: which revolution does it relate to? When and where? What was the result?
questions.answer:
• (a) The French Revolution (post-revolution Napoleonic Wars).
  • (b) 1805, at Austerlitz in central Europe.
  • (c) Napoleon defeated the combined forces of Austria and Russia.
